newsitem.title: UK: EUROPEAN TOURISM TO BENEFIT FROM EMU, SURVEY SAYS.
newsitem.headline: EUROPEAN TOURISM TO BENEFIT FROM EMU, SURVEY SAYS.

text.p: The introduction of a single European currency will create both winners and losers in Europe's travel industry but will encourage overall growth in tourism, a survey by the Centre for Economics and Business Research (CEBR) said on Tuesday.

The survey, carried out for the Association of British Travel Agents (ABTA), found that if European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) goes ahead, European economies could perform better, resulting in more travel for both business and leisure purposes.
But if the euro failed to take off, sterling would still be likely to benefit, leading to an increase in the number of Britons travelling abroad.
Chief executive ABTA Ian Reynolds said: "Overall, this is good news for our industry. Although there will be some obvious losers, the euro will stimulate further growth in travel and tourism."
But bureaux de change stand to lose around 180 million sterling ($285.7 million) annually in foreign exchange business if the euro goes ahead.
